n: Frightened advisers urge David to run and hide like a bird in the mountains. David replies that he has already taken refuge in the Lord.

f.w: In the LORD put I my trust
Flee as a bird to your mountain

n: The advisers point out that the wicked are aiming arrows from the shadows at the upright.
“When the foundations of society are crumbling, what can a righteous person do?” It is the voice of discouragement.

f.g: When law, order, and justice collapse.

n: David’s answer: the Lord is still in his holy temple and on his heavenly throne. His eyes see and test everyone.

f.w: The LORD is in his holy temple

f.g: He examines closely, as if narrowing his eyes.

n: The Lord tests the righteous, but he hates the wicked and anyone who loves violence.
He will rain fiery coals and sulfur on the wicked, with a scorching wind as their portion — as at Sodom.

f.g: Their allotted share — the cup they must drink.

n: The Lord is righteous and loves righteousness; the upright will see his face.

f.w: his countenance doth behold the upright
f.g: Or “the upright shall behold his face.”
